title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）
meta: 主题语境：饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）　|　核心词汇：pork　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pork 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the cook ① cooked the pork that no guest in the canteen would have noted, and he said the cooking was the whole of the day. The ② pork, meaning the meat itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed unnoted in the book; pork, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ spoonful of pork in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ pork at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Pork, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the cook said the noting is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pork was the whole of the matter, meaning the food and not the meat. The ⑥ pork, meaning the food and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; pork, he said, is either something you cook or the only word that means both meat and a food. He said the food is the part they remember.

By 1989 the ⑦ pork had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ pork of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of noting; pork, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pork I remember is the pork noted in the menu, which closed in 1991 and is still noted as the quietest in the canteen. ⑩ Pork, my mother said in 1993, is the only thing that improves by being noted; all pork, she said, is a food that has agreed to look like meat. She said the food was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 猪肉（指食堂里每一勺旁边的那一勺）
B. n. 猪肉（指那块猪肉本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：cook the pork 烧这一块猪肉
D. n. 猪肉（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 猪肉之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的猪肉之事）
F. n. 猪肉（指菜单里写到、被记下的那一块）
G. n. 猪肉、荤腥（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 荤腥（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cooked the pork that no guest in the canteen would have noted
The pork, meaning the meat itself and not the bowl
Every spoonful of pork in that canteen
the pork at the far table
the pork was the whole of the matter
the pork had become a line in a menu
The pork of the whole thing

answers.why: cook the pork 意为“烧这一块猪肉”，1984 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯记下的一块猪肉做了一遍。
pork 意为“猪肉”，指那块猪肉本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被记下。
pork 意为“猪肉”，指食堂里每一勺旁边的那一勺，每一勺旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
pork 意为“猪肉”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pork 意为“猪肉、荤腥”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这块荤腥就是那件事的全部。
pork 意为“荤腥”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那块猪肉，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pork 意为“猪肉”，指菜单里写到、被记下的那一块，到 1989 年这一块成了菜单里的一行。
pork 意为“猪肉之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的猪肉之事是一处食堂和三个日子的记下。
pork 意为“猪肉”，我记得的是菜单里记下过的那一块，1991 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一块。
pork 为抽象总称，母亲 1993 年说，猪肉是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的猪肉。
